title: VernLLM adds retries, fallback and rate limits without a separate gateway
friendlyTitle: VernLLM helps apps recover when an AI service fails
summary: VernLLM is a typed TypeScript call layer that wraps existing model clients with timeouts, retry budgets, circuit breaking, provider fallback, caching and local rate limits. It runs inside the application, supports major providers and adds no runtime dependencies of its own.
friendlySummary: VernLLM adds retries, backup providers, time limits, caching and traffic limits around existing AI connections. It runs inside a TypeScript application instead of through another network service.
whyItMatters: Production AI calls fail in ordinary ways—timeouts, throttling and provider outages—so resilience belongs in the design rather than in emergency patches. An in-process library suits individual services; teams needing central policy across many languages may still prefer a gateway.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI services sometimes slow down or stop working. These controls can keep one failed call from breaking the whole app, although larger organisations may still want one shared gateway.
